label: Thesis: Shade and Sponge (Porta)
text: Barcelona will replace more than half of its plane street trees within ten years, and the only documented rule for the replacement species is qualitative (district, sidewalk width, tradition); no rule quantifies heat or runoff. Can a trait-based layout method, working inside Barcelona's replacement rules (15% species cap, tree size class set by sidewalk width), choose replacement species for the plane trees of Porta (Nou Barris) that retain more pedestrian cooling and storm-water interception than the city's own rule-based replacement? Heat is measured as mean UTCI over 12-17 h on a hot design day, from crown shade and leaf area index; runoff as event volume from a 2-year 60-minute design storm with canopy interception and SCS curve number on a 1 m grid with D8 flow routing, using LiDAR-derived crown size and LAI per tree. A multi-objective optimiser compares heat-best and runoff-best layouts and the trade-off between them.
